Explanation of the words:

*Tabtaghi mardat azwajik* (seeking the pleasure of your wives): that is, by forbidding her.

*Qad faradha lakum tahillata aymanikum* (Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths): that is, He has prescribed for you the means of releasing yourselves from them through the expiation mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah.

*Hadithan* (a statement): it is the forbidding of Maariyah and his saying to her, "Do not disclose it."

*Falamma nabba'at bihi* (And when she divulged it): that is, Hafsah told Aishah, and I tested her with it, thinking that there was no harm in doing so through her own ijtihad (independent reasoning).

*Wa adhharahu Allahu alayhi* (And Allah made him aware of it): that is, He informed him of it, meaning of the matter that had been divulged.

*Arrafa ba'dahu* (He made known part of it): that is, to Hafsah.

*Wa a'rada 'an ba'd* (And he overlooked part): that is, out of the generosity of the Prophet (ﷺ).

*In tatuba ila Allah* (If you two turn in repentance to Allah): that is, Hafsah and Aishah, may Allah be pleased with them both, your repentance will be accepted.

*Faqad saghat qulubukuma* (Your hearts have certainly inclined): that is, they inclined toward forbidding Maariyah, meaning that this pleased you.

*Wa in tazahara alayhi* (And if you two support one another against him): that is, you cooperate against the Prophet (ﷺ) in what he dislikes.

*Fa inna Allaha huwa mawlahu* (Then indeed Allah is his protector): that is, his helper.

*Wa salih al-mu'minin* (And the righteous of the believers): that is, Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.

*Wal-malaikatu ba'da dhalika zahir* (And the angels thereafter are his supporters): that is, they are his helpers and assistants.

*Qanitat* (devoutly obedient): that is, worshipful.

*Sa'ihat* (wandering): that is, fasting, or emigrating.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: "O Prophet, why do you forbid that which Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful" (66:1). This is a rebuke from Allah, the Exalted, to His Messenger (ﷺ) for having forbidden his slave-girl Maariyah in order to please his wives. The reason was that he (ﷺ) was alone with her in the house of one of his wives, and she saw him, and said, "O Messenger of Allah, in my house and on my bed!" So he made her forbidden to himself in order to please the owner of the chamber and the bed. Then Allah revealed these verses containing this story, saying: "O Prophet, why do you forbid that which Allah has made lawful for you," meaning his slave-girl Maariyah the Copt, mother of Ibrahim. "Seeking the approval of your wives," that is, seeking their pleasure. "And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful" toward you, so there is no blame or rebuke upon you after this, and your slave-girl is not forbidden to you, and expiate your oath, since he had said, "She is forbidden to me, and by Allah I will not approach her."

As for His words, "Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths": that is, the means by which you release yourselves from your oaths when you swear, and this is what is mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah in His words: "Its expiation is feeding ten needy persons with the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. But whoever cannot find [the means], then fasting three days. That is the expiation for your oaths when you have sworn" (5:89). His words, "And Allah is your Protector," mean the one who manages your affairs and your helper. "He is the All-Knowing of the conditions of His servants, the All-Wise in His decree and His management of His creation."

As for His words, "And when the Prophet confided": that is, remember when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement, and she was Hafsah bint Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, when he said to her, "Indeed, so-and-so is forbidden to me, and by Allah I will not approach her," and he asked her not to disclose this secret.

She then told Aishah, with whom she was close and affectionate.

Allah informed His Messenger of that. So when she divulged it, and Allah made him aware of it, he made known part of it to Hafsah and overlooked part, out of his own generosity (ﷺ). She said, "Who informed you of this?" He said, "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me." As for His words, "If you two turn in repentance to Allah," that is, Hafsah and Aishah, "your hearts have certainly inclined," that is, they inclined toward forbidding Maariyah, meaning this pleased you. The answer to the conditional is understood as: your repentance will be accepted. As for His words, "And if you two support one another against him," that is, cooperate against him (ﷺ) in what he dislikes, then indeed your cooperation, O Hafsah and Aishah, may Allah be pleased with you, will not harm him at all, for Allah is his protector, and Jibril, and the righteous of the believers, Abu Bakr and Umar, and the angels thereafter are his supporters, that is, his helpers and assistants, against anyone who harms him or intends him evil.

As for His words, "It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you": in this there is a severe warning to the Mothers of the Believers and a great divine discipline for them, for He promised His Messenger that if he divorced them, He would replace them with better than them, "Submissive, faithful, devout, repentant, worshipful, wandering," that is, fasting or emigrating, "previously married and virgins," meaning some of them previously married and some virgins. However, the Messenger (ﷺ) did not divorce them, and Allah did not replace them, so they are his wives in this world and his wives in the Hereafter.

Furthermore, I point out that there is great disagreement among the people of tafsir regarding what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade upon himself, and for which his Lord rebuked him, and which Allah made lawful for him: is it a drink he loved, or is it his slave-girl Maariyah? It is possible that it is other than what has been mentioned, because Allah did not mention the kind of what His Messenger forbade upon himself, but said only, "Why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you." The majority hold that what was forbidden was Maariyah, while in al-Bukhari it is reported that it was honey, and Allah knows best. Therefore I seek Allah's forgiveness, lest I have said about Him or His Messenger what does not please them. I seek Allah's forgiveness, I seek Allah's forgiveness, I seek Allah's forgiveness; indeed my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of his prophethood (ﷺ) and his complete humanity.

2- Al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on them, derived from this verse that whoever says to his wife, "You are haram (forbidden)" or "I have forbidden you," without intending divorce, must pay only the expiation of an oath. 3- The honour of the Messenger (ﷺ) before his Lord.

4- The virtue of Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 66, verses 9–12:

Explanation of the words:

"Jahid al-kuffar" (strive against the disbelievers): i.e., with the sword.

"Wal-munafiqin" (and the hypocrites): i.e., with the tongue.

"Waghlut 'alayhim" (and be harsh with them): i.e., be firm with them in address and do not deal with them gently.

"Fakhanatahuma" (but they betrayed them): i.e., in religion, since they were both disbelievers.

"Falam yughniya 'anhuma" (so they did not avail them): i.e., Noah and Lot, against their wives.

"Min Allahi shay'an" (anything from Allah): i.e., anything of the punishment of Allah, even if little.

"Imra'at Fir'awn" (the wife of Pharaoh): i.e., Asiya bint Muzahim, who believed in Moses.

"Ahsanat farjaha" (who guarded her chastity): i.e., she guarded it, so that men could not reach it, neither by marriage nor by fornication.

"Fanafakhna fihi min ruhina" (so We breathed into it of Our spirit): i.e., We breathed into the sleeve of her garment through the agency of Gabriel, who is called the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus).

"Wasaddaqat bikalimati rabbiha" (and she confirmed the words of her Lord): i.e., concerning her son Jesus, that he is the Word of Allah and His servant and messenger.

Meaning of the verses:

In the first verse [9], Allah, Exalted is He, after addressing His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) by the title of prophethood as an honour and dignification, commands him to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites. The disbelievers are to be fought with the sword, and raids are to be launched against them until they submit; the hypocrites are to be confronted with harsh speech, eloquent language that frightens and carries threat and warning. His words, "﻿And be harsh with them," mean: press your pressure upon both groups, upon the hypocrites with the tongue and upon the disbelievers with the spear. "Their refuge is Hell, and evil is the destination," if they die upon their hypocrisy and disbelief, or for whom Allah knows their death will be upon that.

In the second verse [10], Allah set forth an example of the disbeliever's failure to benefit from the kinship of a believer, whatever the degree of kinship in his eyes. It is the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot, for each of them was under a prophet and messenger, yet they betrayed them in their religion, so they were disbelievers. The wife of Noah would expose the secret of whoever believed in her husband and inform the tyrants of Noah's people about it, so that they would seize him; and she used to tell them that her husband was mad. The wife of Lot was a disbeliever and would guide the criminals to the guests of Lot when they alighted at his house, at night by means of fire and by day by means of smoke. Since they were disbelievers, their kinship through marriage did not avail them anything. On the Day of Resurrection it will be said to them: "Enter the Fire with those who enter," from the people of Noah and the people of Lot. This is one example, and there is another concerning the believer not being harmed by the kinship of a disbeliever, however strong the marital kinship may be. That other example is the wife of Pharaoh, the disbelieving, wrongdoing tyrant; Asiya bint Muzahim had believed in Moses along with those who believed. When Pharaoh learned of her faith, he ordered her killed. When she learned of the tyrant's resolve to kill her, she said in her supplication to her Lord: "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deed, which is disbelief and wrongdoing, so that I may not be a disbeliever in You nor a wrongdoer toward anyone of Your creation, and save me from the wrongdoing people," that is, from their punishment. Her hands and feet were bound so that a great rock would be dropped upon her if she persisted in faith. She raised her gaze to the sky and saw her house in Paradise, and her soul departed out of longing for Allah and for her house in Paradise, and she had seen it. The rock reached her after her soul had departed, and Allah saved her from the punishment of killing that Pharaoh and his wicked disbelieving gang had intended for her.

As for the words of Allah, "And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity": Allah, Exalted is He, joined Mary to Asiya so that the example would consist of two believing women, just as the first example consisted of two disbelieving women. So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: "And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity against men," at a time when prostitution and fornication had spread throughout the lands of the Children of Israel, just as is the situation today in the lands of the Jews and their like, where hardly any woman is safe from fornication. Yet this did not harm Mary, since she was chaste and pure. Rather, Allah honoured her, because she guarded her chastity, by sending to her His Spirit, Gabriel, peace be upon him, and commanding him to breathe into the sleeve of her garment. The breath, by the power of Allah Exalted, entered her body, and she conceived Jesus, who was by the word of Allah "Be," and so he was, in the moment the breath reached her; and she bore him immediately, as an honour from Allah to she who guarded her chastity, out of fear of Allah and seeking nearness to Him. The spread of vice and fornication around her did not harm her so long as she was pure, just as the disbelief of Pharaoh did not harm the pure Asiya. And just as the faith and righteousness of Noah and Lot did not benefit their two disbelieving, treacherous wives.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "No wife of a prophet ever committed adultery." He spoke truly, for by Allah, no wife of a prophet ever committed adultery, owing to Allah's protection of His prophets. How then would He disgrace or humiliate them? Far is Allah above disgracing or humiliating His friends. Therefore the betrayal mentioned in His words "but they betrayed them" means betrayal in religion and the disclosing of secrets.

As for His words, "and she confirmed the words of her Lord": i.e., His laws and His books which He sent down to His messengers; and she was "of the devout," i.e., obedient to Allah, humbly submitting to Him and lowly before Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of striving against the disbelievers with the sword and against the hypocrites with the tongue, and the duty of the rulers of the Muslims to carry this out, since they are the successors of the Prophet (ﷺ) over his community.

2- Establishing the principle: "No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another." Thus the disbeliever does not benefit from the believer on the Day of Resurrection.
